# Contrast verification (GATE-CONTRAST)

Tool: `design/tools/check-contrast.mjs` — WCAG 2.1 relative-luminance formula
([W3C definition](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG21/#dfn-contrast-ratio)).

Thresholds: normal text **4.5:1** (WCAG 1.4.3 AA), non-text UI components and
meaningful graphics **3:1** (WCAG 1.4.11).

Result: **130/130 pass, 0 fail.**

The system deliberately holds even 'muted' text to the 4.5 text threshold rather than the 3.0 large-text relaxation. Low-contrast body text is the classic failure mode of terminal-inspired UIs and is banned here.

## Declared exemptions

- **`color.border.subtle`, `color.border.default`, `color.chart.grid`** — Purely decorative separators and gridlines. They never carry information on their own: every row, card and chart datum is also distinguished by spacing, a label, or a token from the checked set. WCAG 1.4.11 does not apply to purely decorative boundaries.
  - Compensating control: Wherever a boundary is load-bearing (focused input, selected row, table header rule), the design uses color.border.strong / color.border.accent / color.focus.ring, all of which ARE checked at the 3.0 non-text threshold.
- **`color.bg.scrim`, `elevation.glow.accent`, `elevation.card`, `elevation.overlay`** — Translucent overlays and shadows. Their contribution is not a fixed foreground/background pair; legibility is guaranteed by the surface tokens composited above them, which are checked.
- **`color.focus.ring against a filled control`** — The focus ring is never drawn flush against the control it belongs to: components set `outline: 2px solid var(--cbx-color-focus-ring)` together with `outline-offset: 2px`, so the ring's adjacent colour is always the page or card background, not the button fill.
  - Compensating control: The ring-vs-background pairs (color.focus.ring on color.bg.app and on color.bg.surface) ARE checked at the 3.0 non-text threshold, which is the pairing WCAG 1.4.11 actually evaluates for a detached indicator.
